results.title: A 360 review of AI agent benchmarks - IBM Research
results.content: # A 360 review of AI agent benchmarks. In a survey of 120 AI agent evaluation methods, researchers at Hebrew University, IBM, and Yale summarize recent trends and identify four ways testing could be improved to advance the field. The benchmarks for evaluating this new fleet of LLM agents are evolving, too. To get a bird’s eye view of this changing landscape, IBM researchers joined colleagues at Hebrew University and Yale to review 120 frameworks for evaluating LLM agents. Researchers summarize key trends and notable gaps in what may be the most comprehensive survey of AI agent benchmarks to date. ## The future of AI agent evaluation. The researchers identified four ways that evaluation could be improved to make AI agents safer, more robust, and performant. One benchmark, Gray Swan AI’s AgentHarm, tries to coax agents into overriding their guardrails to do things like jailbreak an AI system or commit fraud, while IBM’s new ST-WebAgentBench simulates high-risk business applications in which safety and trustworthiness are especially critical.

results.title: ICML 2025 Workshops
results.content: The topics we would like to cover are:- Learning Algorithms --- which new architectures and learning techniques (e.g. memory mechanisms for extended tasks, exploration strategies) can enhance the intrinsic ability of computer use agents to acquire, represent, and refine knowledge?- Orchestration --- what novel frameworks or control methods (e.g. dynamic task planning, modular coordination, multi-agent systems) can efficiently manage and integrate multiple learning components to optimize overall agent performance?- Interfaces --- how should agents perceive and act within their environments (e.g., via APIs or UI interactions), and should we design unified systems or specialized agents for different modalities?- Guardrails, safety \& societal implications --- what guardrails do we need in order to make computer use models safe for deployment ``in the wild'' while ensuring that they have a positive impact on society?- Benchmarking \& tools --- how can we develop robust environments and evaluation metrics that capture the diversity of real-world settings?

results.title: A generative multi-agent framework for multimodal fusion in few-shot ...
results.content: MALM-CLIP is a pioneering generative multi-agent framework for few-shot anomaly detection that leverages large language models to autonomously generate prompts and text labels, enhancing detection efficiency and accuracy without manual prompt engineering. Compared to traditional methods that rely on manually crafted prompts, MALM-CLIP significantly improves the accuracy and efficiency of few-shot anomaly detection by fully automating the prompt creation process, thereby advancing the field of multimodal information fusion. We propose MALM-CLIP, a generative multi-agent framework for few-shot anomaly detection that automatically generates prompts and text labels using large language models, eliminating the need for manual prompt engineering while improving recognition efficiency and accuracy. The proposed MALM-CLIP is a GenAI-driven method for few-shot industrial anomaly detection, integrating an enhanced CLIP model, a multi-agent collaborative system, and a semantic connection enhancement module to achieve robust multimodal information fusion. We presented MALM-CLIP, a novel anomaly detection method that integrates multi-agent systems with large language models (LLMs) to enable robust multimodal information fusion in few-shot scenarios.
